title: Why does HDR to SDR look grey and washed out?
fullTitle: FFmpeg HDR to SDR: a Plain Conversion Puts 100 Nit White at 127, Not 235

scenes.narration: You convert HDR to SDR with a plain dash pix underscore fmt, and it looks grey and washed out. Why? We build a ten bit PQ clip with ten grey patches of known brightness, and measure what the conversion does to each.
captions: HDR to SDR looks grey and washed out. Why?
Ten grey patches of known brightness, measured.

scenes.narration: The clip is ten bit, tagged bt two thousand twenty and S M P T E twenty eighty four, which is PQ. Ten grey patches from zero to ten thousand nits. The control is an ordinary SDR clip. Readers: raw luma in Node, ffmpeg signalstats, and ffprobe for the tags.
captions: 10 bit, bt2020, smpte2084. Patches: 0 to 10000 nits.
Readers: raw luma in Node, signalstats, ffprobe tags.

scenes.narration: Plain dash pix underscore fmt only rescales ten bit codes to eight bit. A hundred nit white lands at Y one twenty seven; an S D R white is two thirty five. The fifty nit patch is sixty seven point five codes too dark. Nothing is clipped: the ten thousand nit patch reaches two thirty five. It is just in the wrong place.
captions: Mid-tone error 64.5 codes. Nothing clipped, all misplaced.

scenes.narration: The tags survive: ffprobe still says PQ. So a reader that trusts them can fix it: zscale brings the patches back within half a code. Scale with an output matrix changes nothing useful. The colorspace filter refuses PQ. Force it, and the pixels stay the same but the tags now say bt seven oh nine.
captions: Tags kept: zscale recovers within 0.5 code.
Forced colorspace: same pixels, tags say bt709.

scenes.narration: Zscale alone is exact from zero to a hundred nits, but every patch from two hundred three nits up lands on two fifty five: five highlights, one value. Add tonemap hable and they stay apart: one eighty two, a thousand at two thirty five, four thousand at two fifty four. The control SDR clip stays exactly on its values.
captions: zscale alone: 0 to 100 nits exact, 203 and up all 255.

scenes.narration: Read the color transfer with f f probe first. If it says S M P T E twenty eighty four, use zscale with a tone map. Not tested: real footage, HLG, Dolby Vision, saturated colors, players, other builds.
captions: Not tested: real footage, HLG, Dolby Vision, colors, players.
